DiscordWe ping you when a tier list changes or a new banner drops.JoinZenless Zone Zero 3.2, “Their Secret Histories,” launches on September 9, 2026. The update introduces the new Armorer specialty, adds S-Rank agents Claret and Roxy across two banner phases, and gives players access to free Angels of Delusion outfits through version events. HoYoverse confirmed the date and full update lineup in its official Version 3.2 announcement. The patch will release simultaneously on PS5 and PS5 Pro, Xbox Series X|S, Xbox Cloud Gaming, Xbox PC, Windows PC, Steam, iOS and Android. Zenless Zone Zero 3.2 goes live on September 9. HoYoverse has not yet published the maintenance timetable or the final download size, so players should wait for the in-game maintenance notice before planning around server downtime. The platform list includes every current global version of the game: Players preparing for the new banners can use our Zenless Zone Zero Pity Calculator to estimate pulls and Polychrome costs before Claret and Roxy arrive. Claret is an S-Rank Electric agent and the first member of the new Armorer specialty. She is the Administrative Director of Flint Workshop and the head of the Flint family, with a kit that turns defensive investment into offensive damage. Armorer agents are built around the balance between attack and defense. The specialty adds two mechanics to Zenless Zone Zero: Maim and multi-CRIT. Claret builds Gash on enemies through her attacks. Once the effect is fully stacked, certain skills trigger Maim for extra damage and grant a Laceration damage boost. Her abilities use DEF as their base damage multiplier, making DEF part of her direct damage calculation rather than a purely defensive stat. Her multi-CRIT mechanic activates when CRIT Rate exceeds 100%. The excess rate can produce additional critical hits calculated through Laceration damage, while part of her starting CRIT DMG is converted into CRIT Rate. HoYoverse therefore points to DEF, CRIT Rate and CRIT DMG as the three central build stats for Claret. Armorer agents can also trigger Counter Assists against certain enemy control skills, contesting the attack and pushing the target back. Claret and her signature W-Engine will headline the first half of Version 3.2. Roxy, Flint Workshop’s chief smith, is an S-Rank Wind Stun agent. Her core mechanic creates Eyes of the Storm through a held EX Special Attack, leaving tornadoes on the battlefield that she can gather and detonate. Combining those storm effects produces a larger tornado, while her Ultimate generates several tornadoes for a wide frontal strike. Roxy and her exclusive W-Engine will arrive in the second half of the update. The rerun schedule is split in the same order: HoYoverse has not announced the exact phase-change date. The in-game Signal Search schedule will provide the final start and end times for each banner. Zenless Zone Zero 3.2 begins a two-patch outfit campaign for the Angels of Delusion. By completing related events during Versions 3.2 and 3.3, players can collect faction-series outfits without buying them from the store. The 14-day “Surprise Screening Plan” check-in lets players select one Angels of Delusion outfit after completing its required visits. The “Clink, Clank, Pinball Knight!” event offers another outfit through the Angels Support Operation page once its Challenge Mode is cleared. Version logins will also award a total of 10 Encrypted Master Tapes and 10 Boopons. These are separate from the event outfits and give players ten limited-banner pulls plus ten Bangboo searches over the patch. Check our Zenless Zone Zero codes page for currently active livestream and promotional codes before the update launches. “Their Secret Histories” sends the Proxies to Vyrium, a special zone within the Shrouded Reef, as they continue treating the mutated power inside their body. The investigation reveals that TOPS has already infiltrated Roscaelifer. At the same time, a shipment of Porcelloy disappears from a transfer station. Claret and Roxy investigate the missing cargo and draw the Proxies into a case connected to a covert research facility and Helios Academy. Lindverne Sunbringer, Administrative Director of the Airspace Patrol Department, asks Claret to investigate Porcelloy leads in the remnants of Girtablullu. HoYoverse is framing the chapter around old classmates, a reunion after years apart and secrets Sunbringer has kept hidden. Beyond the pinball event, Zenless Zone Zero 3.2 adds the virtual pet event “Diary of an Orbie Parent,” the Booastrum detective event “Chronicles of the Hobbling Crow,” and the HIA combat event “Shadow Chase Showdown.” Rewards include Polychromes, Tuning Calibrators and other upgrade materials. Enigma of the Labyrinth: Operation Bagel receives a standard seasonal update. It adds new Z-Rank valuables, character Gear, advanced challenges, refreshed server rankings and seasonal missions. Claret and Roxy also join the mode with new Tactical Prisms, Armorer Gear and exclusive Hollow Zero equipment. A new Break-Even Beacon can send a Bangboo away with part of the collected supplies before extraction. Those items still count even if the run fails, reducing the risk attached to a bad evacuation. HoYoverse says a larger themed season with new maps, systems and high-difficulty challenges is still in development. The Beginner Guide expands to include Jane, Hugo and Soldier 0 – Anby. Players who did not claim their Version 3.1 self-select Agent can choose one after the 3.2 update, then select the matching exclusive W-Engine after completing the Phase 2 missions. Koleda receives an enhancement, and Perfect Assist signals become more consistent: golden flashes will trigger Defensive Assist, while red flashes will trigger Evasive Assist. The VR Training Room also gains an Armorer-specific training stage. For the broader roster picture before the new specialty arrives, see our Zenless Zone Zero tier list and the main Zenless Zone Zero hub. The publisher continues to target a 2026 release, although it has not announced an exact launch date. The official Google Play page went live under Bandai Namco Entertainment and was updated on August 26. The game’s official website lists both iOS and Android, but an App Store pre-order is not available through the global site at the time of publication. Mirrors High is not presented as a retelling of Ichigo Kurosaki’s original journey. Bandai Namco describes it as a new story that begins after BLEACH: Thousand-Year Blood War, with familiar Soul Reapers appearing alongside an original cast. Those new characters were designed by series creator Tite Kubo. Ichigo, Rukia and other returning characters will use their original Japanese voice actors, while players take a more personal role through an avatar of their own. The premise centers on the Soul Society and a new threat emerging after the war. Bandai Namco has not yet published a complete chapter outline or confirmed which returning characters will be playable at launch. The Google Play description outlines a three-character squad system. Players combine attack cards during battle, then build toward larger Soul Drive attacks rather than controlling a single fighter for every encounter. Bandai Namco also confirms avatar appearance options and Zanpakuto customization. The store copy links those systems to the player’s progression through the new story, suggesting that the custom Soul Reaper is more than a menu profile. The game is free to download and includes in-app purchases, including random items. The publisher has not revealed banner rates, pity rules, launch characters or pre-registration reward milestones, so none of those systems can be confirmed from the current store page. Android users can register directly through Google Play and receive the normal store notification when the game becomes available. The page does not display a release date or installation size. For iPhone and iPad, Bandai Namco still names iOS as a supported platform on the official site. However, there is currently no global App Store link alongside the Android button. Players should therefore treat Google Play as the only confirmed live pre-registration storefront for now. The original teaser used a summer 2026 window, while the latest coverage and store rollout continue to place the game in 2026. Bandai Namco has not narrowed that to a specific day, and Google Play does not provide a public date. We are keeping BLEACH Mirrors High in the undated 2026 section of the Gacha Release Calendar. That entry will move as soon as Bandai Namco publishes a launch notice rather than a storefront estimate. Mirrors High arrives after a mixed period for licensed mobile games. It is a separate project from KLab’s BLEACH: Brave Souls and the now-closed BLEACH Soul Puzzle, with Bandai Namco handling the new game’s publication. Our Bandai Namco company page tracks the publisher’s active and closed gacha titles. The regional and global status of older BLEACH games is also recorded separately in our service tracker. The new storefront rollout confirms the global version for iOS, Android, PS5 and Windows PC, but Elementa still has not announced a release date. This is an expansion of the campaign rather than the first day of global pre-registration. Elementa opened registration through the official Silver Palace website in May 2025; the August 28 announcement adds platform-specific store pages where players can reserve or follow the game. The buttons are not identical across stores. Apple and Google offer mobile pre-registration, while Sony and Epic currently use their normal wishlist systems for games marked as coming soon. The official website remains a separate registration route. The PlayStation Store page identifies Silver Palace as a PS5 game and lists PS5 Pro enhancements, DualSense vibration and Game Help support. It also states that online play is required and that optional in-game purchases are included. On PC, the Epic Games Store page lists Windows support and marks the game as coming soon. Steam and Xbox versions have not been announced, so the new campaign should not be read as confirmation for either platform. Apple currently displays January 31, 2027 as an expected release date. That date comes from the App Store listing, not from an Elementa announcement, and the other official storefronts continue to show no date. App Store pre-order pages require developers to provide an expected date and can be changed before release. For that reason, Gacha Go! is keeping Silver Palace listed as TBA in the Gacha Release Calendar until Elementa confirms a launch date directly. Silver Palace is a free-to-play open-world action adventure RPG set in Silvernia, an industrialized city shaped by the discovery of Silverium. Players take the role of a returning detective, investigate crimes and conspiracies, and switch between party members during real-time combat. NetEase’s urban open world RPG launches globally on January 15, 2027, a date the team confirmed with a dedicated trailer during gamescom Opening Night Live and now carries in the title of its official website. The announcement did two things at once. It closed the question that had followed the game since it stopped being Project Mugen, and it opened pre-registration, which the official site now runs with a live counter of sign-ups. There is no staggered regional rollout in the announcement: the date given is a global one. The site is also further along than a placeholder: it already carries sections for Characters, Locations and Milestones, which is not what a studio puts up eighteen months out. Ananta is built by Naked Rain and described by its own site as an urban open world RPG where you play as a variety of characters across a city of business districts, hidden alleyways, quiet tea towns and busy old streets, assembling a team as you meet its cast. That is the pitch the game has been making since its first showings, and it is the reason it kept turning up on most-wanted lists without a date attached. Now it has one, and it lands in the middle of January, which puts it at the head of the 2027 calendar rather than buried in the December rush. The wait has been long enough to be worth measuring: we covered the game when it was still called Project Mugen, again when its offline technical tests ran in China, and again days ago when it returned to gamescom with new gameplay footage. The Ananta release date is the piece that was missing from all three. Founder and Chief Editor of Gacha Go!
